gaps.sentence: If you ___ me tonight, I will send you the files first thing.
gaps.explanation: A realistic future condition uses the present simple after 'if': email.

gaps.sentence: If he ___ so stubborn, we would have reached an agreement by now.
gaps.hint: present cause with a result up to now
gaps.explanation: An unreal present cause can produce a result reaching into the past; formally 'were' is used: were not.

gaps.sentence: If I had known you were coming, I ___ a cake.
gaps.hint: unreal past result, would have participle
gaps.explanation: The result of an unreal past condition is 'would have' plus the past participle: would have baked.

gaps.sentence: If the taxi ___ in five minutes, we are going to miss our flight.
gaps.hint: real future risk in the if-clause
gaps.explanation: Real future conditions take the present simple in the if-clause: does not arrive.

gaps.sentence: In your position, I ___ for a written contract.
gaps.explanation: Giving imaginary advice uses 'would' for an unreal present: would ask.

gaps.sentence: He wishes he ___ harder at school when he had the chance.
gaps.hint: past regret, wish plus past perfect
gaps.explanation: Regret about past behavior takes the past perfect after 'wish': had worked.

gaps.sentence: If we ___ tickets today, they will cost half the price.
gaps.explanation: The condition is present simple; only the result clause uses 'will': book.

gaps.sentence: Unless the tickets ___ within a week, ask for a refund.
gaps.hint: unless plus present before an imperative
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' clauses take the present simple, even before an imperative result: arrive.
